question: Does requesting single-line compact JSON preserve the complete native invoice contract and reduce usable analysis latency?
answer: No. The first candidate calibration omitted the explicitly supplied customer name and email. The frozen course stopped after two requests; no timed invoice pairs or missing-price control ran.
cost_interpretation: Calibration is cold-baseline then warm-candidate and fails completeness; its timings are not a comparative speedup.

grounding_errors.message: No client email found; PayPal needs a recipient email to send an invoice.

portable_source_course.cost_scope: Transfer, digest verification, pinned blob acquisition, private runtime and actual Ledgerly model requests; no warmup.

course.materialization_policy: RCLONE_LOCAL_NO_SET_MODTIME=true for this owned receiver; original content and executable modes are verified unchanged before serving.
course.error: Calibration did not produce the expected grounded invoice

source_receiving.reason: Compose the already-merged per-charge decision repair before the first model request; comparison plan and presentation-only condition are unchanged.
source_receiving.materialization: Fresh local timestamps; unchanged verified source bytes and file modes

frozen_plan.purpose: Same complete invoice contract, same native path and decoding schema; compare the existing JSON presentation with a single compact-format instruction.
frozen_plan.decision: Retain every first original request, complete raw response, native application and setup/cleanup cost. Run the missing-price control before the timed invoice pairs; if either condition loses its blocking errors, stop the comparison and address the actual invoice error. Adopt the formatting instruction only if every complete invoice retains all charges, recipient, currency, terms, reported payment, note where specified, and unchanged native grounding, with at least 20 percent lower matched mean and median native-analysis wall times. Any incomplete candidate prevents adoption. Report schema/body equality excluding only the one inserted presentation instruction. Calibration timings are separate because the first includes model loading. Six timed cases use balanced condition order. The five earlier messages are retained regression inputs, and Juniper Field School is an already observed audience input; none is called unseen.

body.prompt:
You extract invoice data from a freelancer's job email.
Return only one JSON object matching this JSON Schema:
{"type":"object","properties":{"client_name":{"type":["string","null"]},"client_email":{"type":["string","null"]},"currency":{"type":["string","null"]},"line_items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"desc":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":["number","null"]},"unit_price":{"type":"string","enum":["15"]},"currency":{"type":["string","null"]},"unit":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["desc","qty","unit_price","currency","unit"]}},"due_days":{"type":["integer","null"]},"due_date":{"type":["string","null"]},"amount_paid":{"type":"number"},"confidence":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},"issues":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"field":{"type":"string"},"severity":{"type":"string","enum":["error","warning","info"]},"message":{"type":"string"}},"required":["field","severity","message"]}}},"required":["client_name","client_email","currency","line_items","due_days","due_date","amount_paid","confidence","issues"]}
Use decimal strings for unit_price.
Rules: never invent an email address or price that is not in the text; use null and add an
issue instead. Quoted earlier messages (lines starting with '>') are history, not scope.
Extract the current client's name and email, including the current From header
when it identifies the client; an explicit bill-to instruction takes priority.
Do not omit an explicit recipient or use one from quoted earlier messages.
desc names the work; put counts, unit rates and currency in their separate fields.
Copy each stated unit rate exactly; never divide a quoted hourly rate by the quantity.
qty is the stated number of units, including number words. Do not use 1 for
multiple hours or hide the quantity only in desc. Use 1 only for a single flat fee.
Omit optional or explicitly excluded work; it is not part of the agreed invoice.
Copy the stated quantity unit (for example hours, pages or days) into unit; use null
when no unit is stated. Never replace hours with a generic item count.
The counted unit is the noun being billed, not a duration or size modifier.
Do not convert the length of a session into hours or days unless that is how it is priced.
A flat fee has quantity 1 and its stated amount as unit_price. Do not calculate
unit_price from a combined total.
Include every agreed separately priced service or fee, even on another line.
Check the entire email for work amounts missing from line_items before returning.
Totals, prior payments and excluded work are not additional invoice items.
If a deposit/partial payment was already made, put it in amount_paid.
Otherwise amount_paid is 0. A quoted fee is not a prior payment.

Net N means due_days N. Copy explicit payment terms, including terms on the work line.
Calendar deadlines use due_date (YYYY-MM-DD) and due_days null; relative terms use due_days and due_date null. Do not infer an absent or ambiguous calendar date.
